item.title: Widespread North American pollution and health impacts from early twentieth century copper production
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01975-9

Mining and industrial emissions can be substantially reduced by technological interventions. The historical case of copper production in Anaconda, Montana shows the widespread health burdens that can result when lax regulation delays such interventions.

item.title: Agricultural data source choice as a dominant control on nitrogen surplus uncertainty
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01992-8

Environmental impacts from nitrogen surplus in agricultural regions make it critical to understand the nature and drivers of excess nitrogen. Bhaduri and colleagues show that data source uncertainty must be accounted for to avoid misalignments in management and mitigation decisions.
item.dc:title: Agricultural data source choice as a dominant control on nitrogen surplus uncertainty
